review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped for consumers of the linearity lemmas and read the laurentCoeffAt_fun_add and laurentCoeffAt_const_mul proofs in LaurentCoeff.lean. I searched Mathlib for a standard bundle that could carry taylorCoeffAt's linearity: a linear-map structure on dslope, or a submodule of functions analytic at a point. I found none. Mathlib's DSlope.lean has no dslope_add or dslope_smul bundle. The only linearity-related lemma there is dslope_sub_smul. Adding a LinearMap would require building a custom analytic-germ submodule or quotient. Only taylorCoeffAt_fun_add and taylorCoeffAt_const_mul have outside consumers (LaurentCoeff.lean 263, 293), and they apply those lemmas by direct rewriting. A bundled map would add coercion overhead there without evidence of a gain. The proofs of taylorCoeffAt_sub and taylorCoeffAt_fun_sum could in principle use map_sub and map_sum, but that benefit is hypothetical. Several lemmas are also unconditional: taylorCoeffAt_const_mul, taylorCoeffAt_neg and taylorCoeffAt_congr. They do not fit a map defined only on analytic germs. Remaining uncertainty: a custom analytic-germ module could be built, but I found no supported use that would justify it under this rubric.
